entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has approached this Court aggrieved by Ext.P5 notice that was served on him, seeking his explanation in respect of certain food items that were seized from his premises which were alleged to be of inferior quality.

While the petitioner submitted his objections to Ext.P5 notice,
during the pendency of the writ petition, Ext.P7 notice was issued to the petitioner by the 2nd respondent, proposing a cancellation of his licence [D & O licence].
It is submitted that, to Ext.P7 notice, the petitioner has preferred Ext.P8 reply before the 2nd respondent, and no orders have been passed thereon.

While so, by Ext.P9 notice, the petitioner was also informed that, on account of the pendency of this writ petition as also the non-finalisation of proceedings, pursuant to Ext.P7 notice, his application for renewal of the licence for the year 2017-18 could not be considered by the respondents.
The petitioner further submits that, against Ext.P9 notice, the petitioner has preferred Ext.P10 appeal and Ext.P11 stay petition before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions.
2. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as also the learned Standing counsel for the respondent Municipality.

On a consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case as also the submissions made across the bar, I find that Ext.P5 notice, that was impugned in the writ petition, initially, was only in the nature of a show cause notice, to which, the petitioner has admittedly submitted a reply [Ext.P6].
Thereafter, during the pendency of the writ petition, the petitioner was served with Ext.P7 notice,
which, again, is in the nature of a show cause notice proposing a cancellation of the licence granted to the petitioner under the Kerala Municipality Act.
To the said notice, the petitioner has preferred Ext.P8 reply, and no orders have been passed by the 2nd respondent, on the said reply, submitted by the petitioner.

The petitioner was also served with Ext.P9 notice, which indicated that his application for renewal of D & O licence could not be considered for the ensuing year, on account of the pendency of the earlier mentioned proceedings.

Taking note of the fact that the petitioner has only been served with notices, and there is no final adjudication, pursuant to those notices, I dispose the writ petition with the following directions:
(i) The 2nd respondent shall consider and pass orders, pursuant to Ext.P7 notice issued to the petitioner, by taking note of Ext.P6 objection filed to Ext.P5 notice, and Ext.P8 objection filed to Ext.P7 notice, within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after hearing the petitioner and others likely to be affected by the orders to be passed by the 2nd respondent.

(ii) The 2nd respondent shall also, simultaneously, and within the period aforementioned, take a fresh decision with regard to the entitlement of the petitioner for a renewal of the D & O licence for the ensuing year.

To enable the 2nd respondent G.S.Brown vs Attingal Muncipality on 8 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13937477/
3 to have a fresh look into the matter, I quash Ext.P9 notice.
The 2nd respondent shall ensure that orders are passed, as directed, within the time granted in this judgment.
The petitioner shall produce a copy of the writ petition along with a copy of this judgment, before the 2nd respondent, for further action.

A.K.JAYASANKARAN NAMBIAR JUDGE prp/16/3/17 G.S.Brown vs Attingal Muncipality on 8 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13937477/
